subject: maths
title: Surface area of prisms and cylinders

scenes.heading: Surface area of prisms and cylinders
scenes.sub: How much wrapping does a solid need?
scenes.say: How much cardboard makes a cereal box, or how much metal makes a drink can? That is surface area. Let’s learn to find it for prisms and cylinders.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Wrapping paper must cover every face of a box
scenes.science: Surface area = total area of all outside faces
scenes.breaks: Real paper overlaps at the folds, so you use a little more than the exact surface area.
scenes.say: Think about wrapping a present. The paper has to cover every face: top, bottom, front, back and both ends. If you unfolded the wrapping flat, its area would be the surface area of the box.

scenes.heading: Unfold it: the net
notes: Six faces in three matching pairs
scenes.say: Here is a box unfolded flat. First the base in the middle, then the front, back, top and two sides around it. The six faces come in three matching pairs, so the surface area is two times l w plus l h plus w h.
scenes.caption: A box unfolded flat: base, front, back, top and two sides. Six faces in three pairs, so SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).

scenes.heading: Any prism
scenes.say: For any prism: two times the area of the end, plus the perimeter of the end times the length. The side faces wrap around the end like a band.

scenes.heading: A cylinder: two coins and a label
scenes.say: Now a cylinder, unfolded. Two circles for the ends, and a rectangle that wraps around. Its length is the circumference, two pi r, and its width is the height. So the surface area is two pi r squared plus two pi r h.
scenes.caption: Two circles for the ends, and a rectangle that wraps around. Its length is the circumference 2πr; its width is h. SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

scenes.heading: Closed cylinder
scenes.question: Find the surface area of a closed cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm.
scenes.say: Radius four, height ten. The two ends are thirty-two pi. The curved surface is eighty pi. Together that is one hundred and twelve pi, about three hundred and fifty-one point nine square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Ends: 2 × π × 4² = 32π. Curved: 2 × π × 4 × 10 = 80π. SA = 112π ≈ 351.9 cm².

scenes.heading: Closed or open?
scenes.say: Always check for a lid. A closed cylinder has two circles. An open one, like a bucket, has only one. The same goes for open boxes: leave out the missing face.

Quick recap. Surface area is the area of the net. For a box, two times l w plus l h plus w h. For any prism, two ends plus perimeter times length. For a cylinder, two pi r squared plus two pi r h. And check for a lid. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: SA = area of the net. Box: 2(lw + lh + wh). Prism: 2 × end + perimeter × length. Cylinder: 2πr² + 2πrh. Check for a lid. Now try the practice questions!
